context.outcome: An authenticated project owner can permanently remove a project and its tasks after an explicit confirmation.
context.scope: A single project owned by the authenticated user, including its project-scoped tasks

useCases.name: Delete an owned project
preconditions: The caller has a valid authenticated Identity session.
The project exists and belongs to the authenticated owner.
The caller explicitly confirms deletion in the client.
The client clearly states that all tasks in the project will also be deleted.
useCases.result: The project and its task records are permanently removed, or a not-found result is returned for a missing or unowned project.

aggregates.name: Project
aggregates.responsibility: Owns a project identity and the lifecycle boundary for project-scoped tasks.
aggregates.consistencyBoundary: Deleting the project removes its dependent tasks atomically through the existing database foreign-key cascade.

valueObjects.name: ProjectId
valueObjects.meaning: Stable identifier of the project selected for deletion.
rules: The API validates the identifier as a UUID before invoking the use case.

valueObjects.name: UserId
valueObjects.meaning: Trusted Identity owner resolved by the API from the authenticated request.
rules: The client cannot choose or override the owner identifier.

policies: Only the authenticated owner may delete a project; missing and unowned IDs share the same not-found outcome.
The client confirmation must identify the project and disclose that all associated tasks are deleted.
The API remains authoritative for ownership and deletion; client-provided task counts are informational only.
invariants: A project delete cannot affect another owner's project.
Project task rows cannot outlive a deleted project; the existing foreign key cascades their deletion.
The UI removes the project from visible state only after the API confirms success.

readModels.name: Project collection
readModels.purpose: Refresh the visible project cards after a successful delete.

boundaries.persistence: ProjectRepository deleteOwned operation; project task foreign key already cascades
boundaries.api: Authenticated DELETE /api/projects/{projectId} contract, UUID request validation, typed command and deleted-project response
boundaries.bff: Projects layer authenticated Nuxt BFF route with validated project ID, CSRF-protected browser mutation, and API error translation
boundaries.client: Starter Nuxt Projects dashboard card action and board context action with confirmation, pending, failure, success, and navigation states
boundaries.identity: Identity session authenticates the caller; API derives trusted owner identity and enforces owner scope
boundaries.runtime: Existing local runtime; no deployment or provider changes

acceptanceCriteria: An owner can open a confirmation modal for a selected project from the dashboard and its task board.
The confirmation names the project and explains that every associated task will be permanently deleted.
Cancel or modal dismissal performs no write; a successful confirmed delete removes the project and cascaded tasks and updates the dashboard.
Missing or unowned project IDs cannot delete data and return the established project-not-found response.
Failed deletes remain visible as an error and keep the project selected/visible for retry.
EN/FR copy, keyboard-accessible Nuxt UI confirmation, pending lock, API tests, BFF/client checks, and browser verification cover the flow.

assumptions.statement: The existing project_id foreign key uses ON DELETE CASCADE, so removing a project permanently removes all associated task rows.
The authenticated user is the only project owner actor in the current Projects API; Identity continues to define authentication while the API enforces project ownership.

problem: The Tasks API and dashboard can create and list projects but cannot remove an owned project; owners need a safe way to retire a project and its associated task records.
invariants: Only the authenticated owner can delete the project.
Deleting the project permanently cascades to its associated tasks.
The UI updates only after the API confirms successful deletion.
decisions: Use hard deletion, matching the existing project-to-task cascade and task-delete semantics; make the cascade explicit in confirmation copy.
Do not accept owner IDs or task counts as trusted API inputs.
Keep deletion in the existing Projects bounded context and do not add a new event, audit log, or undo lifecycle because none exists in this demo contract.
